record.original_question: Can one explore a version of the McKay correspondence over global fields, especially number fields?

evidence.quote: Problem 13.1. Explore the McKay correspondence over global fields, in particular, number fields.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Develop a version of the McKay correspondence in which the base field is a global field, with particular attention to number fields. More precisely, formulate and investigate an analogue of the following picture in the global-arithmetic setting.

Background. Classically, for a finite subgroup $G \subset \mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ acting linearly on $\mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{C}}$, the McKay correspondence relates invariants (cohomological, K-theoretic, motivic, or stringy) of the quotient singularity $\mathbb{A}^n_{\mathbb{C}}/G$ and of its crepant resolutions to the representation theory and conjugacy classes of $G$. A motivic/stringy form of the correspondence expresses the stringy motivic invariant of $[\mathbb{A}^n/G]$ as a sum, over conjugacy classes of $G$ (or over $G$-covers of a formal disk), weighted by a certain "age" or "weight" function. Over a non-closed or positive-characteristic base, the wild McKay correspondence (due to Yasuda and others) replaces the sum over conjugacy classes by an integral over the moduli space of $G$-torsors over a punctured formal disk $\mathrm{Spec}\, K((t))$, using a $p$-adic measure, and connects the resulting invariants to mass formulas counting extensions of local fields.

Problem. Let $K$ be a global field (for instance, a number field) and let $G$ be a finite group. Construct a McKay-type correspondence over $K$ that:
(i) defines suitable arithmetic/motivic invariants of the quotient stack $[\mathbb{A}^n_K/G]$ (and of crepant resolutions of $\mathbb{A}^n_K/G$ when they exist),
(ii) expresses these invariants as a global sum or integral over $G$-torsors over $\mathrm{Spec}\, K$ (or over arithmetic curves over $K$), assembling local contributions at all places of $K$ in a manner compatible with the wild McKay correspondence at each completion, and
(iii) relates the resulting global invariants to the asymptotic counting of $G$-extensions of $K$ ordered by discriminant, in the spirit of Malle's conjecture, and to height-zeta-function-type counts on the quotient in the spirit of the Batyrev–Manin program.

Determine to what extent such a correspondence can be defined, prove its existence in significant cases, and clarify its precise relationship with Malle's conjecture on the distribution of number field extensions with prescribed Galois group.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an exploratory open direction. The wild McKay correspondence has been developed over local fields (in particular over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ and equal-characteristic local fields) by Yasuda and collaborators, and is known to connect with mass formulas and to suggest refinements of Malle's conjecture. However, no published global-field version of the McKay correspondence over number fields has been established; the question remains an open research program.

status_evidence.claim: Existing wild McKay correspondence is formulated over local fields, not global fields.
